mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in WORKPLACES mobility from t-1w to t-0w, coupled with a concurrent increase in RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicates a shift towards more time spent at home, directly reducing discretionary retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the average of the last 28 days, despite WORKPLACES remaining low and RESIDENTIAL remaining high.

mechanism_narrative: The week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC by 4.6 percentage points at t-0w suggests a nascent recovery in consumer confidence and willingness to engage in discretionary activities, which will continue over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 4.0 points week-on-week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than the RETAIL_REC value at t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained positive and increasing GROCERY_PHARM mobility, combined with the recent dip in WORKPLACES, suggests a prioritization of essential errands over discretionary spending, diverting activity away from retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than the average of the last 14 days, while GROCERY_PHARM remains above 10% and WORKPLACES remains below -5%.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp decline in WORKPLACES mobility by 8.7 percentage points at t-0w, following a period of relative stability, indicates a potential re-imposition or tightening of public health restrictions, which will suppress retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES drops by more than 8.0 points week-on-week.
failure_condition: No new restrictions are announced or observed within the next four weeks, and RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Despite the recent drop in workplace activity, the overall trend of TRANSIT mobility remaining slightly positive (above 0%) suggests a baseline level of movement and essential travel that will prevent RETAIL_REC from declining further and may even support a slight recovery over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: TRANSIT mobility falls below 0% for two consecutive weeks within the next four weeks, and RETAIL_REC continues to decline compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained negative values in PARKS mobility (below -20%), combined with the recent sharp drop in WORKPLACES, indicates a general reluctance for outdoor and public activities, which will also negatively impact indoor retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility remains below -20% for two consecutive weeks AND WORKPLACES drops below -10%.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases above -15% within the next two weeks, and RETAIL_REC shows an upward trend compared to the last 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: The increasing trend in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from 4.6% to 12.6% over four weeks), even as other categories fluctuate, suggests that people are still actively leaving their homes for essential needs, creating opportunities for incidental retail and recreation visits if conditions remain stable over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM continues its upward trend (t-0w value is higher than t-1w value).
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM mobility declines in the next week, and RETAIL_REC also declines compared to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: The consistently high RESIDENTIAL mobility (above 6%), especially after the recent drop in WORKPLACES, indicates a strong preference for staying at home, which will continue to suppress any significant recovery in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains above 6% for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility drops below 5% for two consecutive weeks within the next four weeks, and RETAIL_REC shows a sustained increase compared to the last 28 days.
